unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Given $M\in\mathcal M_k$, we observe a random graph with adjacency matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ and its generative progress is given in (1).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The source explicitly reuses the conditional Bernoulli experiment for fixed-M minimax risk. No random latent distribution is imposed on every matrix in the finite parameter class.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: By simple counting, one can show that each entry of $\widehat M$ is a polynomial of entries of $A,\Lambda,B$ with degree at most $2t_1t_2$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Preserve the printed degree claim. Counting the displayed recurrence with eta independent of data gives the generic upper bound 2(t1+1)t2+1 in all A,Lambda,B entries; even counting only A gives 2t1t2+1. The O(log²n) order survives; do not change the original finite bound.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Careful readers may notice that our estimator $\widehat M$ is a low-degree polynomial of entries of $A$ as well as independently generated $\Lambda$ and $B$, while our low-degree polynomial lower bounds in Section 3 are proved for the class of deterministic polynomials. However, this is not an issue since the low-degree polynomial lower bounds will continue to hold if we consider the class of polynomials of $A,\Lambda$ and $B$. This is due to the fact that cumulants on two groups of independent random variables are zero (see Proposition 5 in Appendix B). The same issue has also been dealt with in Claim A.1 by Schramm and Wein (2022).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark1 connects randomized Algorithm1 to deterministic polynomial lower bounds. Its proof reference is not a theorem-statement dependency; appendix bodies remain excluded.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For any vector $v$, define its $\ell_2$ norm as $\|v\|_2=(\sum_i|v_i|^2)^{1/2}$. For any matrix $D\in\mathbb R^{p_1\times p_2}$, the matrix Frobenius and spectral norms are defined as $\|D\|_F=(\sum_{i,j}D_{ij}^2)^{1/2}$ and $\|D\|=\max_{u\in\mathbb R^{p_2}}\|Du\|_2/\|u\|_2$, respectively. The notation $I_r$ represents the r-by-r identity matrix and $\mathbf1_n$ is an all $1$ vector in $\mathbb R^n$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Frobenius norm and all-ones vectors are ambient in Algorithm1. The source’s spectral norm maximization leaves u≠0 implicit; no spectral-norm requirement is imported into T3.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: It has been widely conjectured in the literature that for a broad class of high-dimensional problems, degree-$D$ polynomials are as powerful as the class of $n^D$ (up to $\log n$ factors in the exponent) runtime algorithms (Hopkins, 2018).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The proved lower bounds quantify over polynomial estimators. An inference about all polynomial-time algorithms is conjectural, not an additional proved conclusion of Theorems1–7.

The union appears in minimax proof reductions and Corollary1. Theorem1 ranges over the full Mk; do not replace it by this smaller class or import the proof prior as a premise. The union includes p=q although (13) initially states q<p.

Heuristic small-SNR interpretation following T2, discussed as a generalized Kesten-Stigum threshold. Preserve the exact finite-D conditions in T2 and T5 rather than replacing them with this asymptotic slogan.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: One important feature of Algorithm 1 is that it works for any $p,q\in[0,1]$ and it automatically adapts between situations with a spectral gap or not.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Printed prose claims a broader p,q range than the earlier assortative model q

source_issues.note: Graphon and co-membership losses sum only i<j and divide by binomial(n,2); rectangular loss sums every entry and divides by n1*n2. The source defines Mf_ij=f(xi_i,xi_j) while the sampling model sets diagonal zero; the distinction does not affect off-diagonal loss.

T1,T6 take a supremum over fixed parameter matrices; T2,T5 and T7 average over their stated priors and observation noise. T4 additionally supremizes over arbitrary iid latent-position distributions. Do not introduce balanced labels or a uniform latent law into these scopes.

The model permits q=0 and p=1, but the finite SNR ratios use q(1−p) in the denominator. Nontrivial ratio statements require a positive denominator; the source gives no boundary division convention. T5’s target additionally requires p>q.

The source asserts unique zM even though simultaneous label permutations leave M unchanged. The off-diagonal co-membership matrix ZM is uniquely determined when p>q. The displayed relation for Mij is interpreted off diagonal, as required by the model’s zero diagonal.

Algorithm1 prints B∈R^(p×r), where p is a connectivity probability. Matrix multiplication by the n×n transformed adjacency requires B∈R^(n×r). Preserve the printed source and flag this dimensional typo separately.

T3 sets integer iteration counts t1=t2=C-prime log n without a rounding convention. The printed total degree bound2 t1 t2 misses terms from the displayed recurrence: the generic degree upper bound is 2(t1+1)t2+1 in A,Lambda,B and 2t1t2+1 in A alone with the auxiliary randomness fixed. Both remain O(log²n).

T3 denotes probability by the signal-prior symbol PSBM although its event also involves sampled adjacency and independent Lambda,B. Record the natural joint experiment and this notation ambiguity. The surrounding prose says any p,q∈[0,1], while the referenced prior was introduced under q<p; no unproved scope extension is made.

The PDF’s text layer misreads C-prime,C-double-prime and c-prime as C1,C2 and c1. The census follows the visually printed primes in T3 and T6, preserving the different roles of tuning constants and output constants.

The printed Holder norm uses floor(gamma) derivatives and exponent gamma−floor(gamma), including exponent0 when gamma is an integer. It works on the lower triangle; boundary derivative interpretation is implicit. Do not replace it with another standard Holder convention or silently assert additional boundary extensions.

The parameter-space displays use Q_(zi,zj) while defining separate vectors z1,z2. The prior then prints both vectors as length n, but explicitly indexes rows by n1 and columns by n2. Preserve these typographical inconsistencies and resolve the intended row/column indices separately.

Both row and column labels in PBC are uniform over min(k1,k2), not separately over k1 and k2. The additive observation model states iid standard Gaussian noise; independence from the random signal is the usual intended model but is not separately explicit in that sentence.

The theorems prove lower bounds for degree-constrained polynomial estimators. Equivalence to all algorithms of a given runtime is a conjectural interpretation; the source itself discusses failures of low-degree predictions for certain other problems. No universal runtime lower bound is recorded as proved.

source_claim_references.scope: Full randomized estimator recurrence and auxiliary randomness; T3 supplies tuning and sample size.
Bayes-to-minimax reduction; does not import the homogeneous prior or finite SNR condition into T1.
Smooth graphon lower-bound construction; no homogeneous SBM condition becomes a statement premise and no appendix body is read.
Rearrangement of the graphon lower bound; T5 retains its own explicit SNR condition and co-membership loss.
Gaussian-noise low-degree tools are proof machinery; appendix body excluded.

statement_local_bindings.T1: Integers n,k,D with 2≤k≤sqrt(n), D≥1. Real entrywise polynomial estimates of degree≤D; fixed M in the full symmetric k-class zero-diagonal model; expectation over conditionally independent Bernoulli edges. No class balance or homogeneous prior is assumed.
statement_local_bindings.T2: Assortative homogeneous SBM prior with iid uniform k labels, q
statement_local_bindings.T3: The full randomized Algorithm1 under the specified homogeneous SBM experiment, with auxiliary diagonal Bernoulli(p) and independent Gaussian sketch. r=2k, positive sufficiently large primed tuning constants, log-scale iteration counts, the exact max in eta, and n≥Ck log³n. Bound holds on the stated high-probability event; no low-SNR premise from T2 is inherited. Dimension, rounding and probability-notation ambiguities are recorded.
statement_local_bindings.T4: Gamma>0.5, L>0, polynomial degree D≥1, the printed bounded smooth-graphon class, and every latent distribution Pxi on [0,1]. Expectation integrates iid latent positions and conditional Bernoulli graph. Retain exponent (2gamma+1)/(2gamma+2), not the USVT exponent 2gamma/(2gamma+1).
statement_local_bindings.T5: Same prior/conditional Bernoulli experiment as T2, but target ZM is the zero-diagonal co-membership matrix and loss is off-diagonal pairwise squared discrepancy. Exact general threshold, 1/k−1/k²−3/n bound and in-particular k≤sqrt(n) clause. Numeric labels are identifiable only up to permutations.
statement_local_bindings.T6: Sparse SBM class with 0<rho<1 from preceding definition, 2≤k≤sqrt(n), rho≥c k²/n for some small fixed c∈(0,1), and D≥1. Fixed-matrix worst-case risk under Bernoulli observations; c-prime is a separate lower-bound constant. Preserve the source’s reversed argument order ell(M,Mhat), harmless for the squared discrepancy.
statement_local_bindings.T7: Positive integer n1,n2,k1,k2 and D≥1, 0<r<1, real signal amplitude lambda under the displayed squared threshold. Prior labels on both sides are uniform on the shared min(k1,k2) classes; rectangular iid unit Gaussian observation model. Loss includes all n1*n2 entries. Keep both correction terms and max/min dimensions; no square-matrix, symmetry or Bernoulli assumptions.

ambient_prerequisites: Finite index sets, integers, real multivariate polynomials and total degree; entrywise matrix-valued estimators, infima/suprema and expectations. Parameters fixed before observing data may appear in polynomial coefficients.
Independent Bernoulli edges conditional on a symmetric zero-diagonal probability matrix; independent uniform labels; symmetric measurable probability-valued graphons and iid latent positions.

Euclidean and Frobenius norms, matrix powers, Gaussian sketches, matrix gradient recurrence, all-ones matrices, logarithms, min/max and integer iteration conventions. The step size is parameter-dependent and not computed from the data.

Partial derivatives and the exact printed Holder norm on the lower triangle. Biclustering uses separate row/column labels and iid standard Gaussian observation noise, with independence from the signal understood as the intended additive model.
extraction_policy: Seven full main-text theorem statements. Keep definitions and model-specific scope; preserve explicit source issues separately. Proof-only cumulants, least-favorable constructions, propositions and corollaries are not promoted into theorem statement dependencies. Appendix bodies excluded.
